# Working holiday makers
Check about tax, working and lodging a tax return in Australia if you're a working holiday maker (417 or 462 visa).

## Your residency for tax purposes
### Tax withheld by your employer
#### Example: income below $45,001 for 2020–21 and later income years
If your employer is not registered as a WHM employer, they must withhold tax from your pay using [foreign resident tax rates](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/tax-rates-foreign-residents).

#### Example: tax withheld when working for an employer that isn't a registered WHM employer
As Pamela is not registered as an employer of WHMs, Pamela withholds tax at the foreign resident tax rates starting at 30%.

Aleks is paid weekly and earns $200 a day.

_$1,000 × 30% = $300_

## End of income year or finishing work
### Lodge a tax return
#### Example: income below $45,001 for 2020–21 and later income years

web.title: Employers of working holiday makers (WHMs) | Australian Taxation Office
web.description:
# Employers of working holiday makers (WHMs)
## Register as an employer of working holiday makers
Employers of WHMs must register with us to withhold tax at a special rate.

## Tax rates for working holiday makers
### Registered employers
If they don't, you need to withhold [tax](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/tax-rates-working-holiday-makers) at the top rate.

### Unregistered employers
If you're not registered with us as an employer of WHMs, you must withhold tax at 30% from every dollar earned up to $135,000. For income over $135,000, you need to apply [foreign resident withholding rates](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/tax-rates-foreign-residents).

### High Court decision
Most WHMs are **not** residents for tax purposes.

web.title: Taxation of Australian resident WHMs from NDA countries
web.description:
# Taxation of Australian resident WHMs from NDA countries
## Court decision
### What this decision means for you
#### WHM from a non-NDA country or a non-eligible NDA country or a non-resident from an eligible NDA country
- your employer will continue to withhold tax at the 15% rate

#### WHM from an eligible NDA country and an Australian resident
If we do not accept you are a resident, the [WHM tax rates](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/tax-rates-working-holiday-makers) will apply.

## Vary pay as you go withholding
Your employer will continue to withhold tax from your salary or wages at the rate of 15%.
